requirements.quote:
A Probe Timeout (PTO) triggers the sending of one or two probe
   datagrams when ack-eliciting packets are not acknowledged within the
   expected period of time or the server may not have validated the
   client's address.
requirements.condition: When a PTO is triggered because ack-eliciting packets have not been acknowledged within the expected period or because the server may not have validated the client's address.
requirements.required_behavior: Send one or two probe datagrams.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Complete the PTO action without sending a probe datagram, or send more than two probe datagrams as that PTO action.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can trigger the PTO under either stated circumstance and count the probe datagrams emitted by the endpoint.

requirements.quote:
As with loss detection, the PTO is per packet number space.  That is,
   a PTO value is computed per packet number space.
requirements.condition: When PTO values are maintained for a connection with packet number spaces.
requirements.required_behavior: Compute and maintain a PTO value per packet number space.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use only one undifferentiated PTO value shared across packet number spaces.
requirements.why_checkable: State inspection or timers driven with distinct packet-number-space histories can verify that PTO computation is scoped per space.

requirements.quote: A PTO timer expiration event does not indicate packet loss
requirements.condition: When a PTO timer expires, absent separate packet- or time-threshold evidence of loss.
requirements.required_behavior: Do not treat the expiration event itself as an indication that packets were lost.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Infer packet loss solely from PTO timer expiration.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can expire the PTO while withholding any independent loss signal and inspect whether the implementation enters a loss-indicated state.

requirements.quote:
A PTO timer expiration event does not indicate packet loss and MUST
   NOT cause prior unacknowledged packets to be marked as lost.
requirements.condition: When a PTO timer expiration event occurs and previously sent packets remain unacknowledged.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave prior unacknowledged packets unmarked as lost solely because of the PTO expiration.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Mark any prior unacknowledged packet as lost as a consequence of the PTO expiration event alone.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can expire the PTO with outstanding packets and inspect their loss classification before any other loss-detection event occurs.

requirements.quote:
When an
   acknowledgment is received that newly acknowledges packets, loss
   detection proceeds as dictated by the packet and time threshold
   mechanisms; see Section 6.1.
requirements.condition: When an acknowledgment is received that newly acknowledges one or more packets.
requirements.required_behavior: Run loss detection according to the packet-threshold and time-threshold mechanisms.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Bypass the packet- and time-threshold mechanisms when performing loss detection after the newly acknowledging acknowledgment.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a newly acknowledging ACK and compare resulting loss declarations with the packet- and time-threshold predicates.
